title: pvVisItFLASHReader
body:
## pvVisItFLASHReader

Reads HDF5 checkpoint and plot files of the FLASH multiphysics AMR code. With only "amr_mesh" selected the output is vtkOverlappingAMR; adding particles or diagnostic meshes gives a multiblock dataset. The native pvFlashReader (hierarchical-box AMR) and pvFLASHAMRParticlesReader are the usual choice; use this reader to cross-check them or to get the AMR blocks and particles from one node. FileName takes a list of files, each one time step of a series (ParaView's file-series wrapper).

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The diagnostic meshes are for inspecting the block layout, not physics; leave them unselected.
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrayStatus and CellArrayStatus: the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- The VisIt plugin's own read options stay at their defaults; the ParaView proxy exposes no property to change them.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItFLASHReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItFLASHReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrayStatus` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from FLASH data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The FLASH plugin offers the FLASH unknowns (cell-centred on the AMR mesh) and particle properties (on the particle mesh); which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | The list of files to be read by the reader. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"items":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"minItems":1,"type":"array"}` | `required` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `MaterialStatus` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The FLASH plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `MeshStatus` | Names of the FLASH meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The FLASH plugin reports the block-structured AMR mesh "amr_mesh", a "particles" point mesh when particles are stored, and diagnostic meshes (for example Morton-curve and block/processor meshes). Selecting only the AMR mesh gives vtkOverlappingAMR output. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrayStatus` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from FLASH data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The FLASH plugin offers the FLASH unknowns (cell-centred on the AMR mesh) and particle properties (on the particle mesh); which of them appear here depends on how each is centred in the file. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItFLASHReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": [
      "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
    ]
  }
}
```
